\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{دش} (dush)}{دش (dush)}]{\ar{دش} (dush) — a shower}

\label{lesson:AR-C447-dush}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to greet warmly, then the Arabic for to recommend.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{دش}}
\textbf{\ar{دش}} — \emph{dush} — \textquotedblleft{}a shower\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{أخذت} \ar{دشا} \ar{بعد} \ar{الرحلة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{akhadhtu dushan baʿda ar-riḥla.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I took a shower after the trip.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{دش}} (\emph{dush}) is usually traced to French \emph{douche}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dush}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dush}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{akhadhtu dushan baʿda ar-riḥla.} — I took a shower after the trip.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to greet warmly, then the Arabic for to recommend, then say \emph{dush} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{دش} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A shower\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{مكواة} (mikwāh)}{مكواة (mikwāh)}]{\ar{مكواة} (mikwāh) — a clothes iron}

\label{lesson:AR-C447-mikwah}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to recommend, then the Arabic for a shower.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{مكواة}}
\textbf{\ar{مكواة}} — \emph{mikwāh} — \textquotedblleft{}a clothes iron\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{طلبت} \ar{مكواة} \ar{من} \ar{الاستقبال}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ṭalabtu mikwāh min al-istiqbāl.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I asked reception for an iron.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{مكواة}} (\emph{mikwāh}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{k-w-y}, \textquotedblleft{}to burn with a hot iron\textquotedblright{} (Lane). The tool pattern \emph{mifʿala} names the thing one irons with, beside \emph{kawā}, \textquotedblleft{}to iron\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mikwāh}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṭalabtu mikwāh min al-istiqbāl.} — I asked reception for an iron.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to recommend, then the Arabic for a shower, then say \emph{mikwāh} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{مجفف} (mujaffif)}{مجفف (mujaffif)}]{\ar{مجفف} (mujaffif) — a dryer; a hairdryer}

\label{lesson:AR-C447-mujaffif}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a shower, then the Arabic for a clothes iron.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{مجفف}}
\textbf{\ar{مجفف}} — \emph{mujaffif} — \textquotedblleft{}a dryer; a hairdryer\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{لم} \ar{يعمل} \ar{مجفف} \ar{الشعر} \ar{في} \ar{الحمام}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{lam yaʿmal mujaffif ash-shaʿr fī al-ḥammām.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The hairdryer in the bathroom did not work.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{مجفف}} (\emph{mujaffif}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{j-f-f}, \textquotedblleft{}to be dry\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is the Form II participle, \textquotedblleft{}a thing that dries\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mujaffif}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mujaffif}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lam yaʿmal mujaffif ash-shaʿr fī al-ḥammām.} — The hairdryer in the bathroom did not work.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a shower, then the Arabic for a clothes iron, then say \emph{mujaffif} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{مجفف} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A dryer; a hairdryer\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تعطل} (taʿaṭṭala)}{تعطل (taʿaṭṭala)}]{\ar{تعطل} (taʿaṭṭala) — to break down}

\label{lesson:AR-C447-taattala}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a clothes iron, then the Arabic for a dryer.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تعطل}}
\textbf{\ar{تعطل}} — \emph{taʿaṭṭala} — \textquotedblleft{}to break down\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تعطل} \ar{المصعد} \ar{في} \ar{الفندق}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{taʿaṭṭala al-miṣʿad fī al-funduq.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The lift in the hotel broke down.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يتعطل}, \emph{yataʿaṭṭal}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تعطل}} (\emph{taʿaṭṭala}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ʿ-ṭ-l}, \textquotedblleft{}to be idle, without work\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form V; \emph{muʿaṭṭal}, \textquotedblleft{}out of order\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{ʿuṭla}, \textquotedblleft{}a holiday\textquotedblright{}, share the root.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taʿaṭṭala}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taʿaṭṭala}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taʿaṭṭala al-miṣʿad fī al-funduq.} — The lift in the hotel broke down.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a clothes iron, then the Arabic for a dryer, then say \emph{taʿaṭṭala} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{تعطل} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To break down\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تفقد} (tafaqqada)}{تفقد (tafaqqada)}]{\ar{تفقد} (tafaqqada) — to check on; to inspect}

\label{lesson:AR-C447-tafaqqada}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a dryer, then the Arabic for to break down.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تفقد}}
\textbf{\ar{تفقد}} — \emph{tafaqqada} — \textquotedblleft{}to check on; to inspect\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تفقد} \ar{العامل} \ar{الحمام} \ar{بعد} \ar{العطل}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tafaqqada al-ʿāmil al-ḥammām baʿda al-ʿuṭl.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The worker checked on the bathroom after the breakdown.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يتفقد}, \emph{yatafaqqad}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تفقد}} (\emph{tafaqqada}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{f-q-d}, \textquotedblleft{}to lose, to miss\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form V, \textquotedblleft{}to look for what is missing\textquotedblright{}, and so to check on.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tafaqqada}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tafaqqada al-ʿāmil al-ḥammām baʿda al-ʿuṭl.} — The worker checked on the bathroom after the breakdown.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a dryer, then the Arabic for to break down, then say \emph{tafaqqada} again
\end{itemize}
